title: Maximum Strong Pair XOR I
summary: Given an integer array nums, select two integers that form a strong pair (where the absolute difference between them is less than or equal to the smaller of the two numbers) and have the maximum bitwise XOR value among all such pairs.
statement: Given an integer array nums, select two integers that form a strong pair (where the absolute difference between them is less than or equal to the smaller of the two numbers) and have the maximum bitwise XOR value among all such pairs. Return this maximum XOR value.
constraints: A pair x,y is strong when abs(x-y) is no greater than min(x,y).
The same element may be paired with itself.
Return the maximum bitwise XOR among all strong pairs.
hints: The small source-I constraints permit examining every pair directly.
Check the strong inequality before evaluating a pair.
Keep the largest XOR among qualifying pairs, including each value with itself.
Every permitted pair occurs in the nested scan, so taking their maximum is exact.
editorial: Every permitted pair occurs in the nested scan, so taking their maximum is exact.

tests.explanation: The strong pair three and four has XOR seven, which is maximal.
Only self-pairs qualify, each producing XOR zero.
